ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated in the Cartesian coordinate system, given that the vertices O and B of the rhombus OABC are (0, 0) and (2, 2), respectively, what are the coordinates of the intersection point D of the diagonals of the rhombus after it has been rotated \(135^\circ\) counterclockwise about point O?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the vertices of the rhombus OABC are O(0,0) and B(2,2), the coordinate of point D is found to be (1,1).\\
$\therefore OD=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, the angle between OB and the positive y-axis is $45^\circ$,\\
and the angle between the positive y-axis and the negative x-axis is $90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ when the rhombus is rotated $135^\circ$ counterclockwise around point O, i.e., when line segment OD is rotated $135^\circ$ counterclockwise around point O, OD is then on the negative x-axis,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of the intersection of the diagonals of the rhombus D are ($-\sqrt{2}$, 0).\\
Thus, the answer is: $(−\sqrt{2}, 0) = \boxed{(-\sqrt{2}, 0)}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given the vertices of the rhombus OABC are O(0,0) and B(2,2), the coordinate of point D is found to be (1,1).\\ $\therefore OD=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$, the angle between OB and the positive y-axis is $45^\circ$,\\ and the angle between the positive y-axis and the negative x-axis is $90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ when the rhombus is rotated $135^\circ$ counterclockwise around point O, i.e., when line segment OD is rotated $135^\circ$ counterclockwise around point O, OD is then on the negative x-axis,\\ $\therefore$ the coordinates of the intersection of the diagonals of the rhombus D are $(-\sqrt{2}, 0)$.\\ Thus, the answer is: \boxed{(-\sqrt{2}, 0)}.

Then reason: The problem gives O=(0,0), B=(2,2). A rhombus is also a parallelogram, so the diagonals bisect each other, so D is the midpoint of diagonal OB, D=((0+2)/2,(0+2)/2)=(1,1). When rotating counterclockwise about O by 135°, use the rotation formulas x'=x cos135° - y sin135°, y'=x sin135° + y cos135°. Substitute x=1, y=1, cos135°=-√2/2, sin135°=√2/2, obtaining x'=-√2/2-√2/2=-√2, y'=√2/2-√2/2=0. Therefore the coordinates of the intersection point of the diagonals after rotation are (-√2,0).
